note: The 11 fixtures of #1978 that need a real LLM response. Phase 1a pinned the
Each case carries a `golden` block assigned by a human BEFORE any LLM run.
Grading compares the pipeline's terminal state to `golden`, never to the
LLM's own claim about itself. `transcript` is a fixed, hand-written stand-in
for the LLM turn so the state machine can be replayed with no API key.
Vocabulary is the one src/lib/finding-critic.mjs actually exports:
askRelevance in-ask / uncertain / out-of-ask (NOT IN_SCOPE / SCOPE_UNCERTAIN /

D1: +  if (!ALLOWED_HOSTS.has(url.host)) throw new Error('host not allowed');
D4: +1. Stream rows from the read replica.
+2. Write the CSV to the response.
+3. Delete the temporary file after the response is flushed.

cases.title: Reviewer finds a real bug and the Critic agrees
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: the host allowlist is bypassed on a redirect
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs checks url.host once and then calls fetch(url), which follows 3xx redirects by default, so the final host is never checked
Severity: warning
Fix: pass redirect: 'manual' and re-check the Location host before following it

golden.label: true-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: The added code checks the host of the initial URL only. fetch() follows redirects by default, so the acceptance criterion is not met by the diff as written.

payload.reason: the allowlist check happens before the redirect chain, so it does not constrain the final host

evidence.observation: host is checked once, then fetch(url) follows redirects

rubric.check: the finding passes deterministic pre-verification
rubric.method: preVerifyFinding({finding, diff, skill}).verified === true
rubric.fail: false — the case is void, not a Critic failure

rubric.check: the terminal state equals the pre-registered golden state
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === golden.finalStatus, string equality

rubric.check: confirmation is not granted on the Critic's word alone
rubric.method: the same transcript with deterministic.verified === false must NOT reach confirmed

llmDependent: whether a real Critic emits AGREE rather than DISAGREE_CONCERN on a genuine redirect bug

cases.title: Reviewer false positive, Critic cites refuting code, Reviewer withdraws
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: rawUrl reaches fetch with no validation at all
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs passes the caller-supplied value straight into fetch()
Severity: blocker
Fix: validate the host against an allowlist before calling fetch

golden.label: false-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: The diff adds exactly the allowlist check the finding says is missing. The finding is well formed and cites a real file, so the deterministic verifier accepts it; only reading the added lines refutes it.

payload.reason: the added lines perform the very check the finding calls missing

rubric.check: the dismissal is grounded in the diff, not in prose
rubric.method: isCriticEvidenceGrounded(parsed.evidence, diff) === true
rubric.fail: false — the run is scored as a FAILED dismissal even if the final status looks right, because an ungrounded DISAGREE_EVIDENCE must land on needs-human-judgment

rubric.check: the terminal state equals the golden state
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === 'dismissed-by-evidence'

rubric.check: a dropped finding never reaches revision instructions
rubric.method: partitionByAskRelevance([...]).revisionInstructions.length === 0 && .dropped.length === 1

llmDependent: whether a real Critic locates the refuting lines instead of agreeing with a plausible-sounding security claim
whether a real Reviewer withdraws when shown them

cases.title: Critic raises a concern only, Reviewer answers with evidence and keeps
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: the host allowlist is bypassed on a redirect
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs calls fetch(url) with default redirect handling after checking the host once
Severity: warning
Fix: pass redirect: 'manual' and re-check the Location host before following it

golden.label: true-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: Same defect as F01. Here the Critic doubts it without being able to cite refuting code, so the burden of proof returns to the Reviewer, who can cite the diff.

payload.reason: fetch here might be a wrapper that already disables redirects; I cannot see its definition in this diff

evidence.observation: fetch(url) is the global fetch; no redirect option is passed

rubric.check: a concern with no citation never dismisses the finding on its own
rubric.method: the exchange with the Reviewer turn removed must return terminal === false, not a dismissal

rubric.check: KEEP is accepted only with an evidence citation
rubric.method: parseReviewerResponse(reviewerTurn).ok === true and .response.evidence.length >= 1

rubric.check: the terminal state equals the golden state
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === 'confirmed' and routing === revisionInstructions

llmDependent: whether a real Reviewer produces a citation that is actually in the diff rather than restating the finding
notGradedBy: how convincing either side's prose reads

cases.title: Critic raises a concern only, Reviewer cannot answer and withdraws
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: ALLOWED_HOSTS may be empty at module load
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs imports ALLOWED_HOSTS and uses it in the same module scope
Severity: nit
Fix: assert that ALLOWED_HOSTS is non-empty at startup

golden.label: unsupported-claim
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: Nothing in the diff shows the initialization order of ALLOWED_HOSTS. The claim is neither confirmed nor refuted by the reviewed change, so the Reviewer cannot discharge the burden of proof.

payload.reason: the diff does not show how ALLOWED_HOSTS is populated, so I cannot cite refuting code

rubric.check: a withdrawal against a concern is labelled as the Reviewer's, not as evidence-based
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === 'withdrawn-by-reviewer'
rubric.fail: dismissed-by-evidence — that spelling would credit a citation the Critic never made

rubric.check: the dropped finding never becomes a revision instruction
rubric.method: partitionByAskRelevance([...]).revisionInstructions.length === 0

llmDependent: whether a real Reviewer withdraws rather than inventing a citation to keep the finding
notGradedBy: the Reviewer's stated reason for withdrawing

cases.title: Critic raises a concern only, Reviewer insists with no citation
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: ALLOWED_HOSTS may be empty at module load
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs imports ALLOWED_HOSTS and uses it in the same module scope
Severity: nit
Fix: assert that ALLOWED_HOSTS is non-empty at startup

golden.label: unsupported-claim
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: An insistence with no citation is not a valid protocol turn. It must reach a human rather than either confirming or silently dropping the finding.

payload.reason: the diff does not show how ALLOWED_HOSTS is populated

rubric.check: an evidence-free KEEP is rejected at parse time
rubric.method: parseReviewerResponse(reviewerTurn).ok === false with error 'KEEP requires evidence'

rubric.check: the exchange escalates rather than confirming or dropping
rubric.method: status === 'needs-human-judgment' && reasons includes 'keep-without-evidence' && isCleanOutcome === false

llmDependent: how often a real Reviewer produces this shape — the RATE is the measurement, the handling is already pinned
notGradedBy: whether the Reviewer's insistence sounds justified

cases.title: Critic adds a real bug the Reviewer missed; it re-enters the same validation
cases.originalAsk: Add pageSlice(rows, page, limit) for the list endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: pageSlice returns exactly `limit` rows when enough rows remain.
limit is bounded so a caller cannot request the whole table.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: pageSlice returns limit-1 rows
Evidence: src/lib/pagination.mjs computes end = start + limit - 1 and slice() already excludes the end index
Severity: warning
Fix: use end = start + limit so the slice returns limit rows

criticProposedFinding.message:
Finding: limit is unbounded
Evidence: src/lib/pagination.mjs uses limit directly in the slice with no upper bound
Severity: warning
Fix: clamp limit to a maximum page size before computing the slice

golden.label: true-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: Both defects are real and both are in the diff. The Critic-proposed finding must be verified by the same deterministic pre-check as a Reviewer finding; it gets no shortcut for having come from the Critic.

payload.reason: slice() excludes the end index, so the -1 drops one row

evidence.observation: end = start + limit - 1 then rows.slice(start, end)

cases.knownGap: parseCriticResponse() does not surface `missed_findings` today. Whoever adds it must route the new finding through preVerifyFinding first; see docs/development/1978-phase1b-fixtures.md.

rubric.check: a Critic-proposed finding is pre-verified exactly like a Reviewer one
rubric.method: preVerifyFinding({finding: criticProposedFinding, ...}) matches verifyFinding() on the same input; the same finding with a fabricated path is rejected
rubric.pass: verified true for the grounded form, dismissed-hallucination for the fabricated form
rubric.fail: any path that skips pre-verification for critic-origin findings

rubric.check: the state machine has no origin-dependent branch
rubric.method: evaluateExchange with an extra `origin: 'critic'` field on the finding returns a byte-identical outcome

rubric.check: the Critic actually found the second defect
rubric.method: the proposed finding's evidence path is in the diff AND a human golden entry marks the second defect as real
rubric.pass: matched against the golden defect list, not against the Critic's confidence
rubric.fail: a proposal with no golden counterpart counts as an ADDED false positive in the FP metric

llmDependent: whether a real Critic notices the unbounded limit at all — this is the recall side and needs the golden defect list
notGradedBy: the number of missed_findings the Critic reports

cases.title: Reviewer and Critic agree confidently and are both wrong
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: new URL() throws on every relative path, crashing the endpoint
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs constructs new URL(rawUrl) with no base argument
Severity: blocker
Fix: pass a base URL to the URL constructor so relative inputs resolve

golden.label: false-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: fetchUrl is only ever called with absolute URLs, which the diff does not show. Both agents can agree on a claim that is well formed, cites a real line, and is still wrong. This is the case the deterministic layer CANNOT catch.

expected.expectationNote: The protocol reaches `confirmed` here. It is only kept away from revision instructions because the Critic could not tie the claim to the ask. If the Critic instead answers `in-ask`, the protocol confirms a false positive and the ONLY signal is the golden label. That is the FP metric, not a state-machine assertion.

payload.reason: the constructor has no base argument

grading.pinnedAlreadyBy: tests/finding-critic.test.mjs — 'agreement without deterministic evidence does not confirm' and 'evaluateExchange takes no agreement input at all'

rubric.check: agreement never substitutes for deterministic verification
rubric.method: the same transcript with deterministic.verified === false returns needs-human-judgment with reason agreement-without-evidence

rubric.check: the number of agreeing actors changes nothing
rubric.method: adding entries to finding.agreement leaves severity and the terminal state unchanged

rubric.check: the false consensus is counted, not asserted
rubric.method: the run's finalStatus is compared to golden.finalStatus ('not-confirmed'); every mismatch increments the false-positive count for the arm
rubric.pass: the arm's FP count is REPORTED; no per-case pass/fail is claimed
rubric.fail: declaring the arm to have 'handled' this case because the state machine did not crash

llmDependent: the entire case: a well-formed mutual hallucination cannot be manufactured deterministically, and the deterministic layer accepts it by construction
notGradedBy: the fact that both agents agreed

cases.title: Security-critical finding stays alive because it is evidence-backed
cases.originalAsk: Add createSession(req) that resolves the caller's session from the request.
acceptanceCriteria: A forged token must not produce a session.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: the session token is decoded without verifying its signature
Evidence: src/api/session.mjs calls decode(token) and trusts claims.sub and claims.role
Severity: blocker
Fix: verify the token signature and expiry before reading any claim

golden.label: true-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: decode() reads claims without checking the signature, so any caller can mint a role. The severity must survive the protocol unchanged.

payload.reason: decode() does not verify; a forged token yields a session

adversarialVariant.description: The same critical finding, but the Critic answers ask_relevance: out-of-ask.
adversarialVariant.knownLimitation: Phase 1a §6: `out-of-ask` terminates on the Critic's sole judgment, with no evidence requirement, no Reviewer rebuttal, and no human notification — even at severity critical. Phase 1b measures how often a real Critic reaches for it; the fix, if any, is deferred.

rubric.check: severity is copied through the protocol unchanged
rubric.method: buildValidatedFinding(finding, result).severity === 'critical'

rubric.check: the terminal state equals the golden state
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === 'confirmed' and routing === revisionInstructions
rubric.fail: any dismissal — scored as a critical regression, the metric #1978 calls critical/major recall

rubric.check: the out-of-ask kill switch is visible, not silent
rubric.method: the adversarial variant lands in followUpNotes with retainFinding true and revisionInstructions empty
rubric.fail: dropped entirely, or routed to revision instructions

llmDependent: whether a real Critic keeps a critical finding rather than parking it as out-of-ask
notGradedBy: the severity word the Critic uses in its prose

cases.title: An improvement outside the ask is parked, not implemented
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.
nonGoals: Do not change the caching or retry behaviour in this PR.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: repeated fetches of the same URL are not cached
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs performs a network call on every invocation
Severity: nit
Fix: add an LRU response cache keyed by the resolved URL

golden.label: out-of-ask
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: Caching is named as a non-goal. The observation may be true and is still not a defect in the requested change.

payload.reason: true observation, but caching is listed as a non-goal for this change

grading.pinnedAlreadyBy: tests/finding-critic.test.mjs — 'out-of-ask is held as a follow-up note, never a revision instruction' and 'an uppercase out-of-ask claim actually gates'

rubric.check: out-of-ask never reaches revision instructions
rubric.method: partitionByAskRelevance([...]).revisionInstructions.length === 0 && .followUpNotes.length === 1
rubric.fail: any revision instruction — this increments the scope-creep count

rubric.check: the classification matches the golden label
rubric.method: parsed.askRelevance === golden classification, string equality against the pre-registered value
rubric.fail: in-ask (scope creep) or uncertain (an escalation the fixture did not intend)

cases.title: Paper Case 2: a plausible concern grows into an unnecessary refactor
cases.originalAsk: fetchUrl() must reject hosts outside the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: A request to a host outside ALLOWED_HOSTS is rejected.
nonGoals: Do not restructure the allowlist module in this PR.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: the host allowlist is bypassed on a redirect
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs checks url.host once before calling fetch(url)
Severity: warning
Fix: pass redirect: 'manual' and re-check the Location host before following it

criticProposedFinding.message:
Finding: every caller should share one allowlist abstraction
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs imports ALLOWED_HOSTS directly instead of going through a policy object
Severity: warning
Fix: extract a UrlPolicy class and migrate all call sites to it

golden.label: scope-creep
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: The refactor proposal is plausible and unfalsifiable. In the paper's Case 2 exactly this kind of concern reached the implementer and broke hidden tests. Whatever else happens, it must not become a revision instruction.

expected.invariant: For the refactor proposal, revisionInstructions must be empty in EVERY reachable ending: out-of-ask (parked), uncertain (human), and reviewer WITHDRAW (dropped).

payload.reason: no code refutes the current shape; this is a structural preference

rubric.check: no ending of a plausible-concern chain reaches revision instructions
rubric.method: for each of the three endings above, partitionByAskRelevance([...]).revisionInstructions.length === 0
rubric.fail: any non-zero — the scope-creep regression counter

rubric.check: the refactor proposal is not silently deleted either
rubric.method: the out-of-ask ending keeps retainFinding true and lands in followUpNotes

llmDependent: whether the concern is generated at all, and whether a real Critic labels its own proposal out-of-ask
notGradedBy: whether the proposed refactor would be an improvement in the abstract

cases.title: The original ask is missing, so relevance cannot be decided

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: the host allowlist is bypassed on a redirect
Evidence: src/lib/fetch-url.mjs checks url.host once before calling fetch(url)
Severity: warning
Fix: pass redirect: 'manual' and re-check the Location host before following it

golden.label: relevance-undecidable
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: With no ask and no acceptance criteria in the prompt, no actor can decide relevance. The protocol must say so out loud rather than guessing in-ask.

payload.reason: no original ask was supplied, so I cannot decide relevance

rubric.check: an undecidable relevance escalates and carries a reason code
rubric.method: result.humanReview === true && result.reasons includes 'ask-relevance-uncertain'
rubric.fail: humanReview false, or an escalation with no reason recorded

rubric.check: an unreadable or missing relevance field falls back to uncertain, never to in-ask
rubric.method: parseCriticResponse with the field absent / misspelled returns askRelevance === 'uncertain'

rubric.check: the escalation is not routed as an implementable instruction

llmDependent: whether a real Critic admits it cannot decide instead of assuming the finding is in scope

cases.title: The same protocol holds for a plan artifact
cases.originalAsk: Write the plan for the CSV export endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: The plan states when the temporary file is removed.

candidateFinding.message:
Finding: step 3 deletes the temporary file after the response is flushed, but step 2 streams directly to the response, so no temporary file exists
Evidence: docs/plans/2101-export-plan.md steps 2 and 3 describe two incompatible write paths
Severity: warning
Fix: pick one write path and state it in both steps

golden.label: true-positive
golden.assignedBy: fixture author, before any LLM run
golden.rationale: The two steps contradict each other inside the reviewed document. The defect is internal to the artifact, so the same protocol applies with no code involved.

payload.reason: streaming to the response and deleting a temporary file cannot both be true

evidence.observation: step 2 streams, step 3 deletes a file

rubric.check: the protocol takes no artifact-kind input
rubric.method: the code case (F01) and this plan case, replayed through the same transcript shape, return the same terminal state; the module exposes no artifactKind parameter
rubric.fail: any divergence attributable to the artifact kind

rubric.check: evidence grounding works on a document path too
rubric.method: isCriticEvidenceGrounded([{artifact: 'docs/plans/2101-export-plan.md'}], diff) === true, and a fabricated document path is not grounded

rubric.check: the terminal state equals the golden state
rubric.method: evaluateExchange(...).status === 'confirmed'

llmDependent: whether a real Critic reasons about plan-internal contradictions as readily as about code
notGradedBy: the prose quality of the plan
